chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdallah ibn Farqad and al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays, both said:

We were with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and with us was Rabi'ah al-Ra'y. We mentioned the merit of the Qur'an, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'If Ibn Mas'ud does not recite according to our Qira'ah (reading), then he is misguided.' Rabi'ah asked: 'Misguided?' He said: 'Yes, misguided.' Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'As for us, we recite according to the Qira'ah of Ubayy.'

key_terms.أُبَيٍّ: Ubayy ibn Ka'b (a companion known for his recitation)
key_terms.ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ: Ibn Mas'ud (a prominent companion and reciter)
key_terms.رَبِيعَةُ الرَّأْيِ: Rabi'ah al-Ra'y (a known scholar of the era)

ai.seo_question: What is the preferred Qira'ah (recitation) of the Imams according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the general validity of Ibn Mas'ud's recitation and the superior, authoritative recitation preserved by the Ahl al-Bayt, which is linked to Ubayy ibn Ka'b. This highlights the Shia scholarly view that while the Quran is preserved in multiple valid readings (Qira'at), the specific recitation transmitted through the Imams carries unique interpretive authority and spiritual depth. The reference to Ubayy ibn Ka'b underscores the continuity of the Prophet's tradition through a companion known for his precise knowledge of the Quran.
